newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine wheat sowing to fall over 10 pct-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Argentine wheat sowing to fall over 10 pct-analyst.

text.p: Argentina's 1997/98 bread wheat area will probably fall by more than 10 percent compared with the previous season due to dryness in some areas and to some switching to other crops, a grains analyst said Monday.

Patchy rain fell in wheat areas including southern Santa Fe Monday, but probably not enough to build up depleted soil moisture in the area to levels favorable for sowing, Armando Casalins of the Cereals Elevators Association told Reuters.

"But the question of how much will be sown does not just depend on soil moisture," he said, adding that some farmers in Argentina's wheat heartlands in southern Buenos Aires were considering barley or dhurum wheat.
In some other parts of the country, sowing is still likely to be troubled by the lingering effects of a long drought.
"I'd say they've still got problems in southern Santa Fe. A few drops of rain today won't have done them much good," he said, "Cordoba is in the same shape as Santa Fe."
He forecast a significant drop in sown area from 1996/97.
"Compared with last year's seven million hectares, I'd say it wil fall by a bit more than 10 percent," he said.
In early May, Casalins said he only expected a fall of 3-5 percent in sown area.

The governent's Agricultural Secretariat said May 21 that it expected sowing to fall by between 12.3 percent and 5.5 percent, as long as timely rain relieved moisture deficits in Cordoba, central and southern Santa Fe, and Entre Rios.
Argentine farmers harvested a record 16.1 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97, according to the latest Secretariat estimate.
